target: दरवाज़े के अंदर कोई खड़ा है।
english: Someone is standing in the doorway.
tip: Nouns ending in -आ shift to -ए before position words: दरवाज़ा (darvaaza = door) becomes दरवाज़े के अंदर (darvaaze ke andar = inside the doorway).

target: पोस्ट ऑफ़िस किस गली में है?
english: In which lane is the post office?
tip: कौन (kaun = who) and क्या (kya = what) both become किस (kis) before a position word: किस गली में (kis galee mein = in which lane).

target: स्टेशन के सामने मेरा इंतज़ार करना।
english: Wait for me in front of the station.
tip: 'Wait for me' is मेरा इंतज़ार करना (mera intazaar karna) – literally 'do my waiting'. Hindi says whose waiting it is, not who you wait for.

target: नक्शे के हिसाब से मंदिर उत्तर में है।
english: According to the map, the temple is in the north.
tip: के हिसाब से (ke hisaab se) = 'according to', literally 'by the account of': नक्शे के हिसाब से (nakshe ke hisaab se) = going by the map.

target: स्टेशन जाने के लिए कौन सा रास्ता लूँ?
english: Which route should I take to go to the station?
tip: A verb before के लिए (ke lie = for) takes the -ने form: जाना (jaana = to go) becomes जाने (jaane): स्टेशन जाने के लिए (station jaane ke lie) = to get to the station.

target: कड़ी धूप में बिना छाते के बाहर मत जाओ।
english: Don't go outside without an umbrella in harsh sunlight.
tip: बिना (bina = without) wraps its noun: बिना छाते के (bina chhaate ke = without an umbrella) – bina goes before the noun, ke comes after.

target: आज हमने बिरयानी की जगह पुलाव बनाने का फ़ैसला किया।
english: Today we decided to make pulao instead of biryani.
tip: 'Instead of' is की जगह (kee jagah), literally 'at the place of': बिरयानी की जगह पुलाव (biryaanee kee jagah pulaav) = pulao in biryani's place.

target: बस मेरे ऑफ़िस के सामने ही रुकती है।
english: The bus stops right in front of my office.
tip: Tiny ही (hee) means 'right/exactly': ऑफ़िस के सामने ही (office ke saamne hee) = right in front of the office, that exact spot.

target: दरवाज़े से गुज़रकर हवेली के अंदर गए।
english: They walked through the gateway into the mansion.
tip: से (se) usually means 'from', but with motion it can be 'through': दरवाज़े से गुज़रकर (darvaaze se guzarkar) = passing through the doorway.

target: मंदिर के सामने बाईं ओर मुड़ जाना।
english: Turn left in front of the temple.
tip: An instruction can be just the -ना form: मुड़ जाना (mud jaana) = 'turn' as a gentle command, softer than the direct मुड़ो (mudo). Common in directions.

target: पैसे के बारे में चिंता मत करो।
english: Don't worry about money.
tip: 'About' is three words: के बारे में (ke baare mein), literally 'in the matter of': पैसे के बारे में (paise ke baare mein) = about money.

target: जब तक अंजलि नहीं आती, हम यहीं रुकेंगे।
english: Until Anjali comes, we will stay right here.
tip: Hindi 'until' carries a built-in not: जब तक अंजलि नहीं आती (jab tak Anjali nahin aati) is literally 'as long as Anjali doesn't come'. English has no negative there – Hindi requires the नहीं.

target: अगर तबीयत ठीक रही तो कल ऑफिस जाऊँगा।
english: If I feel well, I'll go to the office tomorrow.
tip: The if-clause looks past: ठीक रही (theek rahi = stayed fine) even though it's about tomorrow. Hindi often uses a past form after अगर (agar = if) for future conditions.

target: जब तुम बाज़ार जाओ तो दूध ले आना।
english: When you go to the market, bring some milk.
tip: दूध ले आना (doodh le aana) looks like 'to bring milk' but works as a command for later: bring it when you go. The -ना form is Hindi's gentle do-it-later imperative.

target: जो चाबी मेज़ पर है, वह मुझे दे दो।
english: Give me the key that's on the table.
tip: Hindi relatives lead: जो चाबी मेज़ पर है, वह (jo chaabi mez par hai, vah) = 'which key is on the table, that one'. The जो clause comes first, then वह picks it up – reversed from English.

target: सपना ने कहा कि वह जल्दी आएगी।
english: Sapna said that she would come soon.
tip: No tense shift in reported speech: कहा कि वह जल्दी आएगी (kaha ki vah jaldi aayegi) = 'said that she WILL come soon'. Hindi keeps the original future where English backshifts to 'would'.

target: जैसे ही ट्रेन आए, मुझे फ़ोन कर देना।
english: As soon as the train comes, give me a call.
tip: जैसे ही ट्रेन आए (jaise hi train aae): the short आए signals the train hasn't come yet. Awaited events in time clauses take this form – not आती है (aati hai = comes) or आएगी (aayegi = will come).

target: चाहे कुछ भी हो, रूबी अपना काम ज़रूर करेगी।
english: No matter what happens, Ruby will definitely do her work.
tip: चाहे कुछ भी हो (chaahe kuchh bhi ho) = 'no matter what', literally 'whether anything even be'. चाहे plus the bare हो covers every possibility at once.

target: अनीता, दरवाज़ा बंद कर दो।
english: Anita, close the door.
tip: बंद कर दो (band kar do) – the added दो (do = give) marks the action as done for someone else. Plain बंद करो (band karo) is the bare order; कर दो adds 'for me'.

target: राहुल, जल्दी तैयार हो जा!
english: Rahul, get ready quickly!
tip: तैयार हो जा (taiyar ho ja) uses the bare stem – the तू (tu) command kept for kids and very close friends. With anyone else it sounds harsh: use हो जाओ (ho jao).

target: अंजलि, ज़रा चाय बना दो ना।
english: Anjali, please make some tea.
tip: A final ना (na) turns an order into coaxing: चाय बना दो ना (chai bana do na) = 'come on, make some tea, won't you'. Here ना pleads – it doesn't negate.

target: कृपया दरवाज़ा बंद कर दीजिए।
english: Please close the door.
tip: The -इए (-iye) ending marks a polite command: बंद कर दीजिए (band kar dijiye) is for people you call आप (aap) – with friends it drops to बंद कर दो (band kar do).

target: सब लोग शांत हो जाइए।
english: Everyone, be quiet.
tip: For states, Hindi commands the change with हो जाना (ho jana = become): शांत हो जाइए (shaant ho jaiye) is literally 'become quiet', not 'be quiet'.

target: कृपया मेरी कुछ मदद कीजिए।
english: Please help me.
tip: करना (karna) has an irregular polite command – कीजिए (kijiye), not kariye: मदद कीजिए (madad kijiye = please help). देना and लेना match: दीजिए (dijiye), लीजिए (lijiye).

target: ऐसा मत करो, ख़तरनाक है।
english: Don't do this, it's dangerous.
tip: Commands say no with मत (mat), not नहीं (nahin): ऐसा मत करो (aisa mat karo = don't do that). नहीं belongs to statements; मत is the don't-word.

target: अपने हाथ धोकर खाना खाओ।
english: Wash your hands and then eat.
tip: Hindi chains steps with -कर (-kar = having done): हाथ धोकर खाना खाओ (haath dhokar khana khao) = 'having washed hands, eat'. One sentence, no 'and then'.

target: दवाई समय पर लेना, मत भूलना।
english: Take medicine on time, don't forget.
tip: A command for later uses the -ना form: दवाई समय पर लेना (davai samay par lena) = take your medicine when the time comes. लो (lo) would mean do it right now.

target: नरेश से कहिए कि कल जल्दी आ जाए।
english: Tell Naresh to come early tomorrow.
tip: Relaying an order: नरेश से कहिए कि (Naresh se kahiye ki = tell Naresh that) + आ जाए (aa jae = he should come). The relayed verb shifts to the should-form, not आओ (aao).

target: कृपया अपनी सीट पर बैठे रहिए।
english: Please remain seated in your seat.
tip: रहिए (rahiye) after बैठे keeps a state going: बैठे रहिए (baithe rahiye) = remain seated. बैठिए (baithiye) alone would invite them to sit down.

target: सुनील जी, कृपया अंदर आइए और बैठिए।
english: Sunil ji, please come inside and sit down.
tip: जी (ji) after a name adds respect: सुनील जी (Sunil ji) is like 'Mr Sunil' but warmer – used for elders, customers, anyone you'd call आप (aap).
